# Andrea Urbani

> Personal website of Andrea Urbani, based in Milan, Italy. He works around technology and entrepreneurship, and has worked across venture capital and startups. The site collects his writing, the resources he keeps updated, and the projects he builds.

## Pages
- [Home](https://andreaurbani.com/): Who Andrea is and where to find him.
- [About me](https://andreaurbani.com/about/): Background, past projects and how he works.
- [Blog](https://andreaurbani.com/blog/): Index of every post.
- [Resources](https://andreaurbani.com/resources/): Index of the resources he keeps updated.
- [Projects](https://andreaurbani.com/projects/): Index of the things he has built.
- [RSS feed](https://andreaurbani.com/rss.xml): Full feed of posts, resources and projects.

## Projects
- [Apex Live](https://andreaurbani.com/projects/apex-live/): A local-first Formula 1 timing wall. It turns the public F1 timing stream into a dense race console with gaps, intervals, sectors and mini-sectors, tyre stints, weather, Race Control, team radio and live championship projections. Every race ever run is mirrored into a local SQLite database for historical context. It runs on your own machine, not on a server, and it is explicit about whether what you're looking at is live, delayed, replayed or synthetic.
- [Media Multiviewer](https://andreaurbani.com/projects/media-multiviewer/): A local-first multiviewer that puts up to four browser tabs or windows on one screen, with one of them chosen as the audio source. Every source is picked through the browser's own screen-sharing panel, so there is no stream URL, API key or account involved. The captured video never leaves the browser: no upload endpoint, no recorder, no proxy, no analytics, no database. It does not bypass DRM, paywalls or access controls, and it is explicit about the sources it cannot show.
